free_tier.stated: Free for up to 5 users and 20 workspaces; the free edition is self-hosted, so storage is bounded by the machine the user runs the server on ('no limitations on storage no matter which plan you’re on')

tooling: Hosted option: P4 Cloud, managed and hosted by Perforce, at $39 per user per month with 64GiB storage included. Free edition: the user installs and runs the P4 server on a rented or free machine (in the cloud or on-premises); no storage limit is imposed by the vendor.
reliability_note: The free edition is a self-hosted server: capacity is the disk of the machine the user runs it on, and the vendor states no storage limit; the free edition is limited to 5 users and 20 workspaces.
confidence_note: documented: the pages read on 2026-11-03 are two vendor pages. https://www.perforce.com/products/p4/free-version-control states that P4 is free for up to 5 users and 20 workspaces and can be deployed in the cloud or on-premises. https://www.perforce.com/products/p4/pricing states that the free version is a self-hosted solution with no limitations on storage, whichever plan. The user and workspace caps and the absence of a storage limit, which decide the verdict, rest on those pages; the identity kind and the interface are not stated on them (the record's own text marks them defaulted).
